text: 其实，要是真的能活在所谓的信息茧房中，可能还是一种幸运。
en: Actually, if you could really live in a so-called information cocoon, it might be a kind of luck.

text: 因为我以前学过一点传播学的东西，了解过【信息茧房】，所以很长一段时间里，自己都在有意无意地避免自己被信息束缚住。
en: Because I previously studied a bit of communication, and understood [information cocoon], for a long time I consciously or unconsciously avoided being bound by information.

text: 但是后来我发现，能一直被推送自己喜欢的东西，未尝不是一种幸福，毕竟生活已经够累了，已经做了够多自己不喜欢的事情，为什么不能有一隅小空间让自己消遣，去看自己喜欢的东西，反而要撕破这层隔绝烦恼、保护自己的茧呢？
en: But later I discovered that being constantly pushed things you like is not necessarily unhappiness. After all, life is already tiring enough, and you have already done enough things you do not like — why can't you have a small corner of space to entertain yourself, to watch things you like, instead of tearing apart this cocoon that isolates troubles and protects you?

text: 不要用信息做坏事，自己消化就可以了(比如不要看到什么引起共鸣的信息就去网爆啥的)。
en: Don't use information to do bad things; just digest it yourself (for example, don't go cyberbully someone just because you see some information that resonates with you).

text: 另外，知识是知识，信息是信息，不要混为一谈。
en: Also, knowledge is knowledge, and information is information — do not confuse them.

text: 用来消遣的，各种碎片化的东西，是【信息】。
en: Things used for entertainment, various fragmented things, are [information].

text: 能帮助自己提升进步的，是系统的【知识】。
en: Things that can help you improve and progress are systematic [knowledge].

text: 从几分钟视频个几篇小短文获得的，是前者。
en: What you get from a few minutes of video and a few short articles is the former.

text: 从书本、论文中甚至是与各种人打交道中获得的，才是后者。
en: What you get from books, papers, and even dealing with various people is the latter.

text: 所以，想娱乐的时候，就去看信息。
en: So, when you want entertainment, go watch information.

text: 想学习的话，就去看知识，知识不会成为困住你的牢笼。
en: When you want to learn, go look at knowledge — knowledge will not become a cage that traps you.

text: 一句老生常谈的话——“学的时候好好学，玩的时候就好好玩”也是这个道理。
en: An old saying — 'study hard when studying, play hard when playing' — is the same logic.

text: 不要硬在娱乐中找知识，这样出发点就是错的，你能指望种下苹果种子长出葡萄吗？
en: Don't force yourself to find knowledge in entertainment; the starting point is wrong. Can you expect grapes to grow from apple seeds you plant?

text: 而且，信息茧房是可以被利用的。
en: Moreover, the information cocoon can be used.

text: 如果你对某个东西很感兴趣，你可以自己多去搜索观看这个东西，让大数据记住你，反而能帮助你培养更大的兴趣，甚至让你从信息开始，对知识产生兴趣，转而去看各种书。
en: If you are very interested in something, you can search for and watch more of it yourself, letting big data remember you; this can instead help you cultivate greater interest, and even let you start from information, become interested in knowledge, and turn to reading various books.

text: 你要是真想学知识，这不也是一个好途径吗？
en: If you really want to learn knowledge, isn't this also a good path?

text: 工具是死的，人是活的。
en: Tools are dead; people are alive.

text: 改变不了环境，但可以利用环境。
en: You cannot change the environment, but you can use the environment.

text: (以上皆为个人看法，不喜勿喷)
en: (All of the above are personal views; if you don't like them, don't flame me.)

text: 观点和我一样 = 觉醒了
en: Views same as mine = awakened.

text: 观点和我不同 = 被洗脑了
en: Views different from mine = brainwashed.

text: 三观正 = 三观正好和我一样
en: Correct values = values that happen to be the same as mine.

text: 当代人不喜欢逻辑和因果；喜欢立场和情绪。
en: Contemporary people do not like logic and causality; they like stances and emotions.

text: 看了一条俄粉内容，就被连续推送“乌军崩溃在即”“普大帝飒爽检阅”“西欧怂了”；看了一条乌粉内容，就会不停收到“20万人大反攻在即”“必将收复全部失地”“俄高层密谋投降”。
en: After watching a pro-Russia piece, you get continuously pushed 'Ukrainian army collapse imminent', 'Emperor Pu dashingly reviewing troops', 'Western Europe chickened out'; after watching a pro-Ukraine piece, you keep receiving '200,000-strong grand counteroffensive imminent', 'will definitely retake all lost territory', 'Russian top brass secretly plotting surrender'.

text: 看了半天，愣是没看出最近哪方在推进战线…
en: After watching for a long time, I still couldn't tell which side has recently been advancing the front line…

text: 你真正支持哪一方的话，难道不是应该很关心他们的软肋短板、忧心忡忡码？
en: If you truly support one side, shouldn't you be very concerned about their soft spots and shortcomings, worried sick?

text: 可惜现在不兴这样思考。
en: Unfortunately, this kind of thinking is not in fashion now.

text: 当前互联网社会放大了西方式洗脑愚民的策略：关怀个体主要聚焦于让其一时情绪好一点。
en: The current internet society has amplified the Western-style brainwashing and dumbing-down strategy: caring for individuals mainly focuses on making their emotions feel a bit better for a moment.

text: 这很顺应人性，但对大家是个温水煮青蛙的长期陷阱。
en: This conforms to human nature, but for everyone it is a long-term trap of boiling a frog in warm water.

text: 而我们中国文化崇尚的“良药苦口利于病”，虽然重视对症、建设性发展，但短期看是反人性的，所以无法被互联网精神鸦片用户喜爱。
en: And our Chinese culture's advocacy of 'good medicine tastes bitter but benefits the illness', although it values targeted, constructive development, in the short term it is anti-human-nature, so it cannot be loved by internet spiritual-opium users.

text: 时代沉疴，一时解决不了，个体只能自救。
en: The chronic illness of the times cannot be solved in a moment; individuals can only save themselves.

text: 要有意识去克服一些人性的弱点，尽量习惯去用“逻辑”“因果”“利弊”看待问题，避免抛开事实不论只顾情绪；以思想和行为去评判人，而不是以标签。
en: You must consciously overcome some weaknesses of human nature, try to get used to looking at problems with 'logic', 'causality' and 'pros and cons', avoid ignoring facts and only caring about emotions; judge people by their thoughts and actions, not by labels.

text: 当然了，很少人可以做到这些。
en: Of course, very few people can do these things.

text: 实际上欧美社会就是这样自动筛选精英和底层的，我们既然现在也难逃影响，那就努力不要被那些搞标签对立情绪煽动的乐色，拖进底层思维。
en: In fact, European and American society automatically screens elites and the bottom tier this way. Since we now cannot escape the influence either, strive not to be dragged into bottom-tier thinking by those trash who stir up label-based opposition and emotional incitement.

text: 一定要记住，有成千上万人相信并点赞评论的东西，不一定就是真的，比如说简中网那么多年最爱传的图之一：
en: You must remember: things believed and liked and commented on by tens of thousands of people are not necessarily true — for example, one of the most circulated images on the Chinese internet over so many years:

text: 而实际上的图片：
en: And the actual image:

text: AAPI指Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders，实际翻译为“亚裔美国人与太平洋岛原住民反对仇视”（并且全大写表示强调语气）
en: AAPI refers to Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, actually translated as 'Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders Against Hate' (and all caps indicate emphasis).

text: 而且在P图的时候还把“美国人不打美国人”写成了繁体中文，实在是太贴心啦
en: And when photoshopping the image, they even wrote 'Americans don't hit Americans' in traditional Chinese — how thoughtful.

text: 评论区还有人已经被石锤打脸了都能想到办法再嘴硬阴阳两句的，看来有的人其实根本就不在乎真相是啥，只要听到的故事能让他们赢，他们就宁愿终身活在信息茧房之中
en: In the comments section, there are even people who, after being conclusively debunked, can still find ways to be stubborn and sarcastic — it seems some people simply don't care what the truth is; as long as the story they hear lets them win, they'd rather live in an information cocoon for life.

text: 不想看内宣N手废料，也不想折腾去海外网络的话，一个好的信息来源是财经要问和快讯
en: If you don't want to read Nth-hand waste from domestic propaganda, and don't want to bother going to overseas networks, a good information source is financial Q&A and flash news.

text: 这类新闻审查较少，基本上和海外媒体同步，要审核也多是事后下架，
en: This type of news is less censored, basically synchronised with overseas media, and even if censored, it is mostly taken down afterwards.

text: 比如财新，金十数据，雪球，财联社
en: For example, Caixin, Jinshi Data, Xueqiu, Cailian Press.

text: 把情绪茧房从信息中剥离开，这可能有些麻烦，但尝试往这个方向去做。
en: Peeling the emotional cocoon away from information may be troublesome, but try to move in this direction.

text: 情绪茧房是个我临时想的词：就是比如你就想看美女跳舞，那你就关注1000个跳舞美女，其它推给你你就点不感兴趣，很快你就有一个茧房了。
en: Emotional cocoon is a term I just coined: for example, if you just want to watch beautiful women dance, you follow 1,000 dancing beauties, and click 'not interested' on anything else pushed to you — soon you have a cocoon.

text: 按原教旨定义它是不是信息茧房，是的，但实际上它不提供信息，你也并不用它获取信息，你只是看美女跳舞爽，所以我把它称为情绪茧房。
en: By the original definition, is it an information cocoon? Yes, but in fact it does not provide information, and you do not use it to obtain information — you just enjoy watching beautiful women dance, so I call it an emotional cocoon.

text: 而很多人的爽点不是看美女跳舞这么简单，他们是需要借助一些信息爽起来的。
en: And many people's pleasure points are not as simple as watching beautiful women dance; they need to use some information to get their pleasure.

text: 或者说「爽」可能也不确切，就是调动自己的情绪。
en: Or to say 'pleasure' may not be quite accurate — it is stirring up one's own emotions.

text: 那么问题来了：这些人的实际需求是找个情绪茧房来满足自己的情绪，但情绪过去是很快的，之后则只有用来引发情绪的信息残留下来了——这才是实质上造成很多人问题的「信息茧房」。
en: Then the question arises: these people's actual need is to find an emotional cocoon to satisfy their emotions, but emotions pass quickly, and afterwards only the information used to trigger the emotions remains — this is the 'information cocoon' that substantively causes problems for many people.

text: 比如最近的TGA例子，开奖前客观信息是「年度游戏获奖的大热门是宇宙机器人，黑神话悟空是第二热门但存在一定差距」，但大量观众需要被满足的情绪是「黑神话输了是意外」，所以这些观众会去寻找，且众多自媒体愿意提供的内容就是这个方向：TGA段子啊，西方话语权啊，索尼塞钱啊，这些是相对比较文明的了。
en: For example, the recent TGA example: before the awards, the objective information was 'the hot favourite to win Game of the Year is Astro Bot, and Black Myth: Wukong is the second favourite but with a certain gap', but the emotion many viewers needed satisfied was 'Black Myth losing was an upset', so these viewers go looking for it, and the content many self-media are willing to provide is in this direction: TGA jokes, Western discourse power, Sony stuffing money — these are the relatively civilised ones.

text: 如果有人被它们满足了情绪，那么他就会更容易记住，并强化自己获知的这些信息——4399小游戏也配？
en: If someone has their emotions satisfied by them, then they will more easily remember and reinforce the information they obtained — is a 4399 mini-game worthy too?

text: 还是TGA例子，我记得大概一个月前，冒出了个「TGA修改规则允许DLC参评」的新闻。
en: Still the TGA example: I remember about a month ago, a piece of news popped up: 'TGA changed its rules to allow DLC to be nominated'.

text: 当然这就是个Q&A，不是啥新规，但不妨碍业务精进的自媒体把它包装成这样。
en: Of course, this was just a Q&A, not a new rule, but that doesn't stop business-savvy self-media from packaging it as such.

text: 因为虽然观众本身不知道这条信息，但它可以满足一个长久存在的情绪需求「总有刁民想害朕」——你允许DLC参评，可不就是想妨碍黑神话拿年度游戏？
en: Because although viewers themselves do not know this piece of information, it can satisfy a long-standing emotional need: 'there are always unruly subjects trying to harm me' — you allow DLC to be nominated, isn't that just to obstruct Black Myth from winning Game of the Year?

text: 仇恨需求也是情绪需求的一种，虽然法环DLC最后啥也没拿（且赔率也一直倒数），但就是得被骂，惨呐。
en: Hatred needs are also a kind of emotional need. Although the Elden Ring DLC ended up winning nothing in the end (and its odds were always at the bottom), it still had to be scolded — how miserable.

text: 这表明了一个非常浅显的事实：满足情绪需求的「信息」和真实世界的「信息」，两者通常都是不兼容的。
en: This shows a very obvious fact: 'information' that satisfies emotional needs and 'information' from the real world are usually incompatible.

text: 如果你用一条信息来满足自己的情绪需求，那就最好不要把它带进真实世界。
en: If you use a piece of information to satisfy your emotional needs, then it is best not to bring it into the real world.

text: 当你看「智能路障」、「直言trigger」这种自媒体来产生情绪共鸣时，你就当自己在看美女跳舞，跳完直接信息清零，毕竟我估摸着看美女跳舞总是记不住什么有效信息的吧。
en: When you watch self-media like 'Smart Roadblock' and 'Zhiyan Trigger' to generate emotional resonance, treat it as watching beautiful women dance — after dancing, directly reset the information to zero. After all, I figure watching beautiful women dance never leaves you remembering any useful information.

text: 当然，上面这段话过于高高在上和没有可行性了，因为如果你要抛开从过往情绪中沉淀下来的信息并寻找新的、真实世界的信息来替换它，要付出不止双倍的努力。
en: Of course, the above passage is too condescending and infeasible, because if you want to discard information settled from past emotions and find new, real-world information to replace it, you have to put in more than double the effort.

text: 所以一个可行的尝试是做一些妥协：不要那么沉迷于满足情绪，但让这些时候获知的信息有那么一丁点用。
en: So a feasible attempt is to make some compromises: don't be so obsessed with satisfying emotions, but let the information obtained in these moments be a tiny bit useful.

text: 这里是有两个大方向的，一个是广开言路，比如有意识搜一些其他信息、反对面的观点等等，但其实能走到这步的，大概也不太容易被信息茧房所困了；另一个其实更难一些但也更基础一些，就是去怀疑那些主动引导你情绪的信息——这应当是不难辨别的。
en: There are two main directions here: one is to open up to more voices, for example consciously searching for other information, opposing views, etc. — but those who can reach this step are probably not easily trapped by information cocoons anyway; the other is actually harder but more fundamental, which is to doubt information that actively guides your emotions — this should not be hard to identify.

text: 该爱了，该恨了，该同情了，该狂欢了——因为它们能调动你的情绪，所以伴随它们的信息，一般都不会特别可靠。
en: Time to love, time to hate, time to sympathise, time to celebrate — because they can stir your emotions, the information accompanying them generally will not be particularly reliable.

text: 我有两句习惯说的话：一曰「什么样的观众配什么样的媒体」，二曰「信息茧房都是自己选的」，也一并放在这里。
en: I have two sayings I habitually use: one is 'what kind of audience deserves what kind of media', and the other is 'information cocoons are all self-chosen' — I'll put them here as well.

text: 能把情绪茧房剥离出来的话，你会同时发现，其实你也能驾驭情绪茧房了。
en: If you can peel the emotional cocoon away, you will also discover that you can actually master the emotional cocoon.

text: 当你想看美女跳舞的时候就去看，想抒发黑神话落选的不甘就去一起喷，甚至想看赢学家们时你都能跟着赢。
en: When you want to watch beautiful women dance, go watch; when you want to vent the disappointment of Black Myth's loss, go rant together; even when you want to watch the 'win-ologists', you can join in the winning.

text: 但回过头面对自己的生活时，你还是知道哪些信息更可靠，这其实是很不错的一件事。
en: But when you turn back to face your own life, you still know which information is more reliable — this is actually quite a good thing.
